Summary
Data source overview: The paper systematically evaluates out-of-distribution (OOD) robustness of 13 NLP model variants (bag-of-words, word-embedding models, and six pretrained Transformers) across seven tasks. It finds that pretrained Transformers trained on large, diverse corpora generalize markedly better to OOD data and detect OOD inputs more reliably than prior models, while model size alone is not a key factor and compression (DistilBERT) can hurt robustness.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]

Inference strategy justification: The paper explicitly reports performance gaps, FAR95 detection scores, and qualitative explanations; these were mapped directly into risk→analysis→insight→design→implementation→evidence. Where authors implied but did not formally phrase an “intervention” (e.g., “use pretrained Transformers”), moderate inference transformed these implications into explicit, actionable safety interventions (confidence marking 2).

Extraction completeness explanation: All core reasoning chains about why OOD degradation occurs and how pretrained Transformers, diverse data, confidence-based detection, and careful compression address these issues were captured. Nodes were merged at a granularity permitting cross-paper de-duplication (e.g., “train-test distribution shift in NLP tasks”). All three high-level safety concerns (performance drop, undetected OOD inputs, robustness loss from compression) terminate in four concrete interventions, forming an interconnected fabric with no isolated nodes.

Key limitations:
1. Validation evidence strength assigned “3” due to limited statistical detail in main text; appendix data might strengthen this.
2. The paper does not provide implementation blueprints for fallback policies, so intervention 22 remains at maturity-2.
3. Connections between spurious cues and detection were inferred; future work could supply direct empirical links.

Suggestions to improve instruction set:
• Clarify how to handle multiple closely related risks (merge vs. separate) to avoid forced fabric inter-connection workarounds.
• Provide an explicit example of edge confidence rationale length expectations.
• Add guidance for citing figure/table IDs in rationales when section titles alone are ambiguous.
